tests.title: An unknown provider value is refused with both accepted values listed
given: a Config with provider = "kubernetes" and no other faults
a gateway factory and a podman factory that count calls
tests.when: Validate / Start is called
then: the joined error contains `sandbox.provider`, `podman` and `gateway`
neither factory is called
tests.pseudocode: err = Start(cfg{provider:'kubernetes'}, counters); assert contains(err,'sandbox.provider','podman','gateway'); assert gwCalls==0 && podmanCalls==0

tests.title: Init with provider gateway against a reachable remote returns a running service
given: an in-process gatewayd.Server with static token T over local on 127.0.0.1:0
a config file with provider = "gateway", gateway_url = http://127.0.0.1:<port>, gateway_token = T and one valid profile
the gateway factory is the real gateway.Dial
tests.when: Init(logger, path, factory) is called
then: the error is nil and the service is non-nil
Service.Provider() is the remote client
tests.pseudocode: svc, err = Init(log, path, dialFactory); assert err == nil; assert svc != nil; assert svc.Provider() != nil

tests.title: No Podman provider is built and no engine binary runs under provider gateway
given: a valid gateway config
a podman factory that fails the test if called
PATH points at a directory containing only a sentinel `podman` script that writes a marker file
tests.when: Init runs to completion against the in-process remote and the service is exercised with one lease Create
then: the podman factory is called 0 times
the marker file does not exist
tests.pseudocode: Init(...); assert podmanCalls == 0; assert !exists(marker)

tests.title: The same profile set is accepted or rejected identically under podman and gateway
given: a table of profile sets: valid, bad max_ttl, bad network_modes entry, CheckSpec-rejected profile
a stub provider reporting identical capabilities for both provider settings
tests.when: Start is called for each set once with provider podman and once with provider gateway (injected factories returning the stub)
then: acceptance or rejection is equal for both providers
for rejections the profile-related message text is identical
tests.pseudocode: for set in sets: e1 = Start(podmanCfg(set)); e2 = Start(gatewayCfg(set)); assert (e1==nil)==(e2==nil); assert profileMsg(e1)==profileMsg(e2)

tests.title: gateway_url and gateway_token are known keys, expanded, and reported in one joined error
given: a TOML file with [sandbox] provider = "gateway", gateway_url = "${GW_URL}", gateway_token = "${GW_TOKEN}" and env GW_URL, GW_TOKEN set
a second file with both keys invalid plus an invalid max_ttl
tests.when: LoadConfig and Validate are called on each
then: the first loads with no unknown-key error and the expanded values are used
the second yields a single errors.Join error naming sandbox.gateway_url, sandbox.gateway_token and sandbox.max_ttl
tests.pseudocode: cfg = LoadConfig(p1); assert cfg.GatewayURL == env(GW_URL); _, err = Validate(LoadConfig(p2)); assert contains(err, three keys)

tests.title: A missing or empty gateway_url under provider gateway is refused as required
given: provider = "gateway" with a valid token
cases: key absent, empty string, ${UNSET} expanding to empty
tests.when: Validate is called for each case
then: each joined error contains `sandbox.gateway_url` and `required`
tests.pseudocode: for c in cases: err = Validate(c); assert contains(err,'sandbox.gateway_url','required')

tests.title: Scheme and parse rules accept loopback http and https and reject the rest
given: provider = "gateway" with a valid token
tests.when: Validate is called with gateway_url values from a table
then: http://127.0.0.1:9000, http://localhost:9000 and https://gw.example:443 pass
http://gw.example:9000, ftp://127.0.0.1 and an unparseable relative value fail with an error containing `sandbox.gateway_url`
tests.pseudocode: for (u, ok) in table: err = Validate(cfg(u)); assert (err==nil)==ok; if !ok assert contains(err,'sandbox.gateway_url')

tests.title: Empty host and out-of-range or non-numeric ports are refused
given: provider = "gateway" with a valid token
tests.when: Validate is called with https://gw.example:1, :65535, :0, :65536, :abc and https://:443
then: ports 1 and 65535 pass
ports 0, 65536, abc and the empty host fail with an error containing `sandbox.gateway_url`
tests.pseudocode: assert Validate(url(':1'))==nil; assert Validate(url(':65535'))==nil; for u in bad: assert contains(Validate(u),'sandbox.gateway_url')

tests.title: Userinfo, query, fragment and non-root path in gateway_url are refused
given: provider = "gateway" with a valid token
tests.when: Validate is called with https://gw.example/, https://gw.example/api, https://gw.example?x=1, https://gw.example#f and https://u:p@gw.example
then: https://gw.example/ passes
the other four fail with an error containing `sandbox.gateway_url`
tests.pseudocode: assert Validate('https://gw.example/')==nil; for u in rest: assert contains(Validate(u),'sandbox.gateway_url')

tests.title: Userinfo is stripped from gateway_url before it is quoted in a failure
given: provider = "gateway" with gateway_url = https://user:pw@gw.example and a valid token
tests.when: Validate is called
then: the error names sandbox.gateway_url
the error contains neither `user:pw` nor `pw@`
tests.pseudocode: err = Validate(cfg('https://user:pw@gw.example')); assert !contains(err,'user:pw') && !contains(err,'pw@')

tests.title: A missing or empty gateway_token under provider gateway is refused as required
given: provider = "gateway" with a valid gateway_url
cases: absent, empty, ${UNSET} expanding to empty
tests.when: Validate is called for each case
then: each joined error contains `sandbox.gateway_token` and `required`
tests.pseudocode: for c in cases: assert contains(Validate(c),'sandbox.gateway_token','required')

tests.title: A 15-character token fails and a 16-character token passes
given: provider = "gateway" with a valid gateway_url
tests.when: Validate is called with tokens of 15 and 16 printable characters
then: the 15-character token yields an error naming `sandbox.gateway_token` and the minimum 16
the 16-character token yields no token error
tests.pseudocode: assert contains(Validate(tok(15)),'sandbox.gateway_token','16'); assert Validate(tok(16))==nil

tests.title: Tokens with spaces, newline or non-ASCII bytes are refused
given: provider = "gateway" with a valid gateway_url
tests.when: Validate is called with 16 valid characters plus `\n`, a token with an embedded space, a token with a tab, and a token with a byte 0x7F or 0x80+
then: each error names `sandbox.gateway_token` and the printable-ASCII-without-spaces rule
a token spanning exactly 0x21 to 0x7E characters passes
tests.pseudocode: for t in bad: assert contains(Validate(t),'sandbox.gateway_token'); assert Validate(allPrintable16)==nil

tests.title: Validation error text never contains the token or any 8+ character substring of it
given: a valid or invalid configuration otherwise, with gateway_url possibly also faulty
tests.when: for any generated gateway_token string (valid, too short, containing invalid bytes, empty), Validate is called
then: for every contiguous substring of length 8 or more of the token, err.Error() does not contain it
tests.pseudocode: for tok in gen_tokens(): err = Validate(cfg(tok)); for sub in substrings(tok, minLen=8): assert !strings.Contains(errText(err), sub)

tests.title: engine_binary, runtime and userns under provider gateway are each refused
given: a valid gateway config plus engine_binary, runtime = "krun" and userns set
tests.when: Validate is called
then: one failure per key, each naming the key and saying it applies only to provider "podman"
e.g. the error contains `sandbox.runtime` and `podman`
tests.pseudocode: err = Validate(cfg); for k in [engine_binary,runtime,userns]: assert contains(err,'sandbox.'+k,'podman')

tests.title: gateway_url and gateway_token under provider podman are refused without echoing the token
given: provider = "podman" with gateway_url set and gateway_token = a known 20-character token
tests.when: Validate is called
then: one failure per key naming it and saying it applies only to provider "gateway"
the error does not contain the token
tests.pseudocode: err = Validate(cfg); assert contains(err,'sandbox.gateway_url','sandbox.gateway_token','gateway'); assert !contains(err, token)

tests.title: Other-provider key failures are collected with other static failures
given: provider = "gateway" with runtime set and max_ttl = "bogus"
tests.when: Validate is called
then: a single error names both `sandbox.runtime` and `sandbox.max_ttl`
tests.pseudocode: err = Validate(cfg); assert contains(err,'sandbox.runtime','sandbox.max_ttl')

tests.title: The gateway factory is called once with exactly the configured URL and token
given: a valid gateway config with a known URL and token
a recording gateway factory returning a stub provider that answers List
tests.when: Start is called
then: the factory is called exactly once
it receives the configured URL string and token string
tests.pseudocode: Start(cfg, recFactory); assert rec.calls==1; assert rec.url==cfgURL && rec.token==cfgToken

tests.title: Start-up issues exactly one List and no Create or Destroy on the remote
given: an in-process remote gatewayd with static token T over a recording wrapper around local
hub configured with the real gateway.Dial and token T
tests.when: Init completes
then: the recording backend observed 1 List, 0 Create, 0 Destroy
the List arrived under hub's token
tests.pseudocode: Init(...); assert rec.lists==1 && rec.creates==0 && rec.destroys==0

tests.title: Static validation failure returns the joined error without building or listing
given: a config with an invalid gateway_url and a recording factory
tests.when: Start is called
then: the factory is called 0 times and no List is issued
the returned error is the joined static error naming sandbox.gateway_url
tests.pseudocode: err = Start(badCfg, rec); assert rec.calls==0 && rec.lists==0; assert contains(err,'sandbox.gateway_url')

tests.title: Factory error, unreachable remote and refused token each refuse start with a scrubbed sandbox: error
given: case A: factory returns an error containing the token and https://user:pw@host
case B: real Dial to a closed 127.0.0.1 port
case C: in-process remote with token A, hub configured with token B
tests.when: Init is called for each case
then: each returns a non-nil error and a nil service
each error starts with `sandbox:` and contains `sandbox.provider`, `sandbox.gateway_url` and `sandbox.gateway_token`
no error contains the token or `user:pw`; case A shows `[redacted]`
tests.pseudocode: for c in cases: svc, err = Init(c); assert svc==nil; assert hasPrefix(err,'sandbox:'); assert contains(err,3 keys); assert !contains(err, token)

tests.title: A remote that never answers List fails start within 11 seconds
given: a gateway factory returning a stub provider whose List blocks until its context is cancelled
tests.when: Start is called and the elapsed time is measured
then: Start returns an error starting with `sandbox:` naming the three keys
the elapsed time is at least 10 seconds and no more than 11 seconds
tests.pseudocode: t0=now(); _, err = Start(cfg, blockingFactory); assert err != nil; assert 10s <= now()-t0 <= 11s

tests.title: The remote client's Capabilities is read exactly once across start-up and later calls
given: a counting stub provider answering List and Capabilities
tests.when: Start succeeds and the hub backend's Capabilities() is then called 20 times
then: the stub's Capabilities was called exactly once in total
tests.pseudocode: svc = Start(cfg, f(stub)); for i in 1..20: backend.Capabilities(); assert stub.capCalls == 1

tests.title: A network_modes entry the remote does not offer refuses start with 25-REQ-5.4's message
given: a remote snapshot offering only ["none"] and a config whose network_modes include "host"
tests.when: Init is called, and the same config is run with provider podman and an identical stub
then: Init returns an error and a nil service
the error text equals the one produced for provider podman
tests.pseudocode: _, e1 = Start(gwCfg, stub); _, e2 = Start(podmanCfg, stub); assert e1 != nil; assert same(e1, e2)

tests.title: A profile rejected by CheckSpec against the snapshot refuses start with the per-profile message
given: a remote snapshot whose capabilities make sandbox.CheckSpec reject one profile
tests.when: Init is called
then: Init returns an error and a nil service
the error names that profile with spec 25's message unchanged
tests.pseudocode: _, err = Start(cfg, stubRejecting); assert err != nil; assert contains(err, profileName); assert equals(msgPart(err), CheckSpec(spec, caps).Error())

tests.title: Backend Capabilities returns the narrowed snapshot while the remote is stopped
given: a service started against an in-process remote offering several network modes
the remote then shut down
tests.when: the hub backend's Capabilities() is called
then: it returns promptly with the narrowed snapshot (network modes limited to hub's configured set)
no call reaches the remote
tests.pseudocode: remote.Shutdown(); caps = backend.Capabilities(); assert caps.NetworkModes == narrow(snapshot); assert rec.calls unchanged

tests.title: A lease followed by Dial and Create produces one box on the remote with the lease's image, TTL and merged env
given: an in-process remote gatewayd (static token T) over a recording wrapper around local.Unisolated
hub service and hub gateway on a second 127.0.0.1:0 with profile `widgets` having env and a resolved secret
tests.when: POST /api/v1/workspaces/widgets/sandboxes, then gateway.Dial(lease.gateway_url, leaseToken) and Create(sandbox.Spec{})
then: the recording backend captured exactly one Spec
its Image and TTL equal the lease's and its Env equals profile env merged with the secrets
the caller received a sandbox handle
tests.pseudocode: lease = post(); c = Dial(lease.gateway_url, tok); sb = c.Create(ctx, Spec{}); assert rec.creates==1; assert rec.spec.Env == merge(profile.env, secrets)

tests.title: Only hub's token reaches the remote and the lease gateway_url is hub's own
given: a remote gatewayd whose authenticator records every token it sees
a lease obtained and a box created through hub's gateway
tests.when: the lease representation is read and the recorded tokens are inspected
then: every token seen by the remote equals hub's gateway_token and none equals a lease token
the lease gateway_url equals hub's own gateway URL and differs from sandbox.gateway_url
tests.pseudocode: assert set(remote.seenTokens) == {hubToken}; assert lease.gateway_url == hubGatewayURL; assert lease.gateway_url != cfg.GatewayURL

tests.title: A second Create is FailedPrecondition and an unminted token is Unauthenticated, without contacting the remote
given: a lease whose caller already made one Create
the remote's recorded Create count is 1
tests.when: the caller issues a second Create under the lease token, and another dial uses a token hub never minted
then: the second Create returns gRPC code FailedPrecondition
the unminted token returns Unauthenticated
the remote records no additional Create
tests.pseudocode: _, e = c.Create(ctx, Spec{}); assert status.Code(e)==FailedPrecondition; _, e2 = bad.Create(...); assert status.Code(e2)==Unauthenticated; assert rec.creates==1

tests.title: DELETE and the caller's Close each destroy the remote box and revoke the lease token
given: two leases each with a box created on the remote
tests.when: DELETE is sent for the first lease, and Close is called on the second lease's handle
then: the remote's List contains neither box
dialling hub's gateway with either lease token is Unauthenticated
tests.pseudocode: del(lease1); sb2.Close(); assert remote.List() empty; assert status.Code(dialCreate(tok1))==Unauthenticated; same for tok2

tests.title: A remote not-found in sentinel form or gRPC NotFound form counts as destroyed
given: a stub remote client whose Destroy returns sandbox.ErrNotFound (wrapped) in one run and status.Error(codes.NotFound) in another
an active lease with a box
tests.when: Backend.Destroy, DELETE and the expiry sweep each run against the stub
then: each treats the box as destroyed and ends the lease as after a successful destroy
DELETE answers its success status, not 502
tests.pseudocode: for form in [sentinel, grpcNotFound]: stub.destroyErr = form; r = delete(lease); assert r.status == okStatus; assert lease.state == ended

tests.title: A remote Unauthenticated or PermissionDenied reaches the caller as Unavailable with one error log
given: a stub remote client returning status Unauthenticated (run 1) and PermissionDenied (run 2) from Create and from Destroy
slog.Default captured by a buffer handler
tests.when: a caller Create is made, then for a second active lease a DELETE is sent
then: the caller sees codes.Unavailable with a scrubbed message
the Create leaves the lease `failed`; the Destroy leaves the lease `active` and DELETE answers 502
exactly one error record per occurrence names `sandbox.gateway_token` and no log contains the token value
tests.pseudocode: e = c.Create(); assert status.Code(e)==Unavailable; assert lease.state=='failed'; r=del(l2); assert r.status==502 && l2.state=='active'; assert count(errorRecords containing 'sandbox.gateway_token') == 2 per run

tests.title: The remote sees exactly one Create per caller Create, including failed ones
given: a recording remote backend with an injectable failing Create
tests.when: one caller Create succeeds and another caller Create fails at the remote
then: the recording backend records two Creates in total, one per caller Create
no Create is retried
tests.pseudocode: rec.failNext(); c1.Create(); c2.Create(); assert rec.creates == 2

tests.title: The scrub set holds the token, the gateway_url string and url.Host under provider gateway
given: a service built with provider gateway, token T, gateway_url http://127.0.0.1:41234
tests.when: provider error text containing T, the URL string, and `127.0.0.1:41234` separately is scrubbed
then: each occurrence is replaced by `[redacted]`
with provider podman the same text is not altered for those values
tests.pseudocode: out = scrub(text, svc.scrubValues()); assert !contains(out,T,url,host); assert contains(out,'[redacted]')

tests.title: A remote error carrying the token and host leaks into no output surface
given: a remote recording backend whose Create returns an error containing hub's remote token and the remote host:port
slog.Default and the audit emitter captured
tests.when: a caller Creates through hub's gateway, then the lease is read over HTTP
then: the gateway error message, lease JSON, HTTP bodies, lease `error` field, audit events and log lines contain neither the token nor the remote host string
the lease is `failed`
tests.pseudocode: rec.createErr = errorf('boom %s at %s', tok, host); e = c.Create(); for out in [e.Error(), leaseJSON, httpBodies, auditEvents, logs]: assert !contains(out,tok) && !contains(out,host)

tests.title: The token is absent from HTTP responses, metrics and the start-up info record, whose attributes are provider and profiles
given: a started service and HTTP server with provider gateway
slog captured
tests.when: the profile listing, an error body (unknown workspace), a lease response and /metrics are fetched and the start-up records are inspected
then: no response body or metric output contains the token
the single start-up info record has exactly the attributes `provider` and `profiles`
tests.pseudocode: for u in urls: assert !contains(get(u).body, tok); rec = infoRecord(); assert keys(rec.attrs) == {provider, profiles}

tests.title: The redacting token renders [redacted] under every formatting and encoding
given: the validated token value and a struct holding it as a field
tests.when: it is formatted with %v, %+v, %#v and %s, logged through slog (text and JSON handlers), and encoded with json.Marshal, both directly and as a struct field
then: every rendering contains `[redacted]` and none contains the token
tests.pseudocode: for f in [%v,%+v,%#v,%s]: out = Sprintf(f, holder); assert contains(out,'[redacted]') && !contains(out,tok); assert !contains(json.Marshal(holder), tok)

tests.title: No start-up error contains the token or URL userinfo
given: a generator of configs (valid and faulty URL, token, other-provider keys, profiles) and of probe failures (factory errors and List errors whose text embeds the token, userinfo and URL)
tests.when: for any generated config and probe failure, Start is called
then: the returned error text never contains the token
it never contains URL userinfo, and any quoted gateway_url has userinfo removed
tests.pseudocode: for cfg, fail in gen(): err = Start(cfg, factoryFailing(fail)); assert !contains(errText(err), cfg.token) && !contains(errText(err), userinfo)

tests.title: Leases and the profile listing keep working while the remote is down
given: a started service whose in-process remote has been shut down
tests.when: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/sandboxes and the profile listing GET are called
then: the lease POST returns its success status
the profile listing returns 200
tests.pseudocode: remote.Shutdown(); assert post(lease).status == 201; assert get(profiles).status == 200

tests.title: A Create while the remote is unreachable fails the lease with a scrubbed error
given: a lease obtained while the remote is shut down
tests.when: the caller dials hub's gateway and calls Create
then: the caller receives an error
the lease state is `failed` and its `error` field contains neither the token nor the remote host
tests.pseudocode: _, e = c.Create(); assert e != nil; l = getLease(); assert l.state=='failed'; assert !contains(l.error, tok, host)

tests.title: DELETE of an active lease while the remote is down answers 502 and changes nothing
given: an active lease with a box, then the remote shut down
tests.when: DELETE is sent for the lease
then: HTTP 502 with error code `sandbox_provider_error`
the lease stays `active` and its token still authenticates at hub's gateway
tests.pseudocode: remote.Shutdown(); r = del(lease); assert r.status==502 && r.json.code=='sandbox_provider_error'; assert lease.state=='active'; assert tokenValid(tok)

tests.title: Close while the remote is down returns an error and leaves the lease active
given: an active lease with a caller handle, then the remote shut down
tests.when: the caller calls Close on its sandbox handle
then: Close returns a non-nil error
the lease state is `active`
tests.pseudocode: remote.Shutdown(); err = sb.Close(); assert err != nil; assert lease.state=='active'

tests.title: The expiry sweep logs a failed destroy and succeeds on the first run after the remote returns
given: an expired active lease with a box on the remote
the remote shut down
slog captured
tests.when: the sweep runs once while the remote is down, the remote restarts on the same address, and the sweep runs again
then: the first run logs one warning or error for the failed destroy and the lease stays active
the second run destroys the box and ends the lease
tests.pseudocode: remote.Shutdown(); sweep(); assert logs(warnOrError)==1 && state=='active'; remote.Restart(); sweep(); assert state=='expired'

tests.title: Hub's next Create succeeds after the remote restarts on the same address without a redial
given: a started service with a counting gateway factory wrapping the real gateway.Dial
the remote shut down and a new gatewayd served on the same 127.0.0.1:<port>
tests.when: a new lease is obtained and the caller calls Create
then: Create returns a sandbox
the factory call count is still 1
tests.pseudocode: remote.Shutdown(); remote2 = serve(sameAddr); sb = c.Create(); assert sb != nil; assert factory.calls == 1

tests.title: The remote client is closed once, after the last shutdown Destroy; a client without Close is fine
given: a stub remote client that records the order of Destroy and Close calls, with two active boxes
a second stub that does not implement io.Closer
tests.when: hub shuts down through the 28 shutdown step and the sandboxes shutdown
then: Close is called exactly once, after the last Destroy
the non-Closer variant shuts down with no error
tests.pseudocode: shutdown(); assert log == [destroy,destroy,close]; assert shutdown(nonCloser) == nil

tests.title: The afc build depends on no agentkit, grpc or internal/sandboxes package
given: go.mod with the agentkit-go replace and the gateway.Dial dependency
tests.when: `go list -deps ./cmd/afc` is run
then: the output contains no agentkit-go, google.golang.org/grpc or internal/sandboxes import path
tests.pseudocode: out = exec('go','list','-deps','./cmd/afc'); for p in [agentkit, google.golang.org/grpc, internal/sandboxes]: assert !contains(out,p)

tests.title: An operator starts hub against a reachable remote agentkit-gateway
given: an in-process remote gatewayd with static token T over a recording wrapper around local on 127.0.0.1:0
a config.toml with provider = "gateway", gateway_url = http://127.0.0.1:<port>, gateway_token = "${AGENTKIT_GATEWAY_TOKEN}" with the env var set, and valid profiles
slog captured
tests.when: Init runs with the production gateway.Dial factory and hub's gateway and HTTP server are then bound
then: Init succeeds
the remote observed 1 List and no Create or Destroy
one info record with attributes provider and profiles only
hub's gateway and HTTP server are listening

tests.title: An agent leases a box on the remote gateway, uses it and deletes it
given: hub started against the in-process remote with a recording backend
a real SQLite lease store, lease API and hub gateway
tests.when: the agent POSTs a lease, dials lease.gateway_url, Creates, and then sends DELETE
then: the box exists on the remote with the lease's image, TTL and merged env
after DELETE the remote's List is empty and the lease token no longer authenticates

tests.title: A remote error carrying hub's token and host is scrubbed end to end
given: hub started against the in-process remote whose Create returns an error containing the token and 127.0.0.1:<port>
logs and audit events captured
tests.when: the agent obtains a lease, calls Create through hub's gateway and reads the lease over HTTP
then: the lease is `failed` with a scrubbed `error` field and an audit event is emitted
the gateway error, HTTP bodies, audit events and log lines contain neither the token nor the host

tests.title: A remote outage fails a lease and hub recovers when the remote returns on the same address
given: hub started against the in-process remote on a recorded 127.0.0.1:<port>
tests.when: the remote is shut down, a lease Create is attempted, the remote is restarted on the same port, and a new lease Create is attempted
then: the first lease is `failed` with a scrubbed error
the second Create returns a sandbox and a box exists on the restarted remote
the gateway factory was called once
real_components: in-process remote gatewayd (two instances on one address)

tests.title: Hub shutdown destroys active boxes through the remote client and then closes it
given: hub started against the in-process remote with one active lease and box
the remote client wrapped to record Destroy and Close order
tests.when: hub is stopped
then: the box is destroyed on the remote
the remote client's Close is called once, after the shutdown Destroy
